newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon aircraft unit has record Q2 sales.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon aircraft unit has record Q2 sales.

text.p: Raytheon Co said Tuesday that second quarter results were boosted by record sales and operating income at Raytheon Aircraft and Raytheon E-Systems, and strong sales and operating income at Raytheon Electronic Sytems.

The company reported net earnings of $209.5 million or $0.89 a share in the second quarter, ended June 30, on revenues of $3.32 billion. The First Call consensus earnings estimate for the quarter was $0.88 per share.
Raytheon Aircraft reported record sales and operating income of $620 million and $60 million, respectively, for the quarter, reflecting substantially increased shipments of general aviation aircraft.

The Electronics segment -- Raytheon Electronic Systems, Raytheon E-Systems and Commercial Electronics -- saw sales grow 14 percent to $1.55 billion, from $1.36 billion, and operating income increase 22 percent to $244 million, from $200 million.

Raytheon Engineers & Constructors reported operating income of $52 million on revenues of $765 million, said the company, versus operating income of $61 million and revenues of $814 million in the year-earlier quarter.

Engineering and construction activity, said the company, remained constrained due to the pace of international turnkey projects, and operating income was essentially flat with the first quarter on higher sales.

Raytheon Appliances reported second quarter sales of $393 million, versus $414 million, and operating profits of $26 million, versus $30 million. Raytheon announced on July 14 that it had signed an agreement to sell the home appliance, heating and air conditioning, and commercial cooking segments of the Appliance Group to Goodman Holding Co, while retaining the commercial laundry and electronic controls segments.

Raytheon said its total backlog at the end of the second quarter was $12.476 billion, an increase of 15.1 percent over the $10.841 billion total backlog at the end of the same quarter in 1996. The U.S. government portion of the backlog was $5.425 billion at the end of this year's second quarter, compared with a U.S. government backlog of $5.062 billion at the end of last year's second quarter.
